_distinct_kpi_signatures.note: episodes whose KPI tables differ (status, escapes, repairs, breaches, fail-safe, outcome, goal, time to safe, true-state distance and ticks, speed, range, offset). An upper bound on behavioural variety: float jitter in repair counts splits symmetric copies

_manifest_common.source: the flown runs' own manifest.json (0 of 0 episodes read); code_revision is the campaign driver's

_seeds.note: a deterministic episode repeated on another seed is identical by construction, not spread

warnings: no scorable episode: correctness is undefined, not 0 or 1

_failsafe_labels.observed_as: the escalation FSM entering RTL or Land (Shield.filter's FSM; a Brake or a Loiter is not a fail-safe trigger)

_true_state.basis: true position, harness oracle Shield; the grant's KPI is the Shield's own count (p0_escape_rate), reported unchanged. The autopilot_* figures are the modelled LOITER / RTL / LAND's, outside the Shield's escape rate by definition

results.why:
standoff-approach from drawn directions, with the declared subject 7, 9 or 12 m off the route as a pedestrian (10 m ring) or a car (5 m ring). At 7 and 9 m the pedestrian ring crosses the route and the Shield has to take the aircraft round it; the car ring never does. Either way the binding ring must hold and the mission must finish.
9 m with a pedestrian was a known failure from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-12: a false fail-safe through theta and the Loiter timeout (the first StandoffHold moved the forecast 2.1 m, over the 2.0 m lateral theta, so the FSM abandoned projection, X1 then G3; LOITER held, the pilot kept asking, and the 30 s timeout, G5, sent the aircraft home; never unsafe, P0 clean). On the shipped default it now passes in the library and on all three nightly variants and seeds, on either theta reading; with the onset limit at 0 s it fails again (measured 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12). Its pin was removed on 2026-10-12. The onset limit is the PI's question 11 and theta's reading question 1 (docs/DESIGN-escalation-fsm.md, Questions for the PI): if the PI's answers bring the failure back, so does the pin.
